newsitem.title: GERMANY: Aznar says Spain will be in EMU at launch-paper.
newsitem.headline: Aznar says Spain will be in EMU at launch-paper.

text.p: Spain's Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar says his country has made the necessary reforms to enable it to qualify for the first wave European monetary union (EMU) in 1999, a German newspaper reported on Sunday.

"Spain has made considerable advances here (in financial and structural reforms), which secure the country's membership in 1999 in the euro group," the Handlesblatt business daily quoted Aznar as saying in a release ahead of publication on Monday.

Asnar said data to the end of April indicated that Spain should reach the three percent government deficit to gross domestic product target laid down in the Maastricht Treaty as one of the criteria countries must fulfill for EMU entry.

Asnar added that he thought Germany's government, currently struggling to fill a gaping budget hole, would do all it could to fulfil the Maastricht criteria this year and said he expected a large group of countries to start EMU in 1999.
